"...using the ends of boards and sticks, and while she was standing there, I do not know what object he used, but he gave her a beating and cut her face in two places. We heard that you, Madam <note>referring to Aunt Xue, Baochai's mother</note>, have a certain medicine here for treating staff wounds. Would you find a pill for me, Miss?"

Baochai heard this and hurried Ying’er to find two pills to give to Ping'er. Baochai said, "Since this is the case, go and give her my regards; I will not go myself." Ping'er assented and departed. Nothing more need be said of this.

It is said that after Xiangling had met everyone and finished dinner, and as Baochai and the others had all gone to Aunt Xue’s quarters, she went by herself to the Bamboo Lodge <note>the residence of Lin Daiyu</note>. By this time, Daiyu was more than half recovered. Seeing that Xiangling had also come into the garden to live, she was naturally pleased. Xiangling said with a smile, "Now that I have come in, I have some free time. If you would only teach me how to compose poetry, it would be my great good fortune!" Daiyu smiled and replied, "Since you want to learn poetry, you must take me as your master. Although I am not an expert, I am generally capable of teaching you." Xiangling laughed, "If that is truly the case, I hereby take you as my master. You must not grow weary of me." Daiyu said, "What difficulty is there in it that it should be so hard to learn? It is nothing more than the <term>qisheng-zhuanhe</term> <gloss>the four steps of poetic composition: introduction, elucidation, transition, and conclusion</gloss>. Within the elucidation and transition, there are two pairs of couplets: level tones must match deflected tones; empty words must match solid words, and solid words must match empty words. If you truly have a brilliant line, it is even permissible to ignore the rules of tonal balance and word types."

Xiangling smiled and said, "No wonder when I used to peek at one or two poems in an old book, some were perfectly matched while others were not. I also heard people say, 'the first, third, and fifth syllables do not matter, but the second, fourth, and sixth must be distinct.' Looking at the poems of the ancients, some follow this smoothly, while others are wrong on the second, fourth, or sixth syllables. I have been confused every day. Now that I hear you say it, it turns out these rules do not matter at all, as long as the phrasing is novel and extraordinary." Daiyu replied, "That is exactly the principle. Phrasing is, after all, a secondary matter; the most important thing is the conception. If the intent and interest are genuine, the poem will be good even without polishing the words. This is called 'not letting the words harm the meaning.'"

Xiangling said, "I only love Lu Fangweng's <note>the Southern Song poet Lu You</note> lines: 'The heavy curtains are not rolled up, keeping the fragrance long; the ancient inkstone is slightly concave, gathering much ink.' It is so vivid and interesting!" Daiyu said, "Because you do not know poetry, you like what is shallow and accessible. Once you enter that mold, you will never be able to break out of it. Listen to me: if you truly wish to learn, I have the <term>Wang Mojie Quanji</term> <gloss>Complete Works of Wang Wei</gloss> here. Take his one hundred five-character regulated poems and study them until you have thoroughly mastered them. Then read one hundred and twenty of Old Du's <note>Du Fu</note> seven-character regulated poems, followed by one or two hundred of Li Qinglian's <note>Li Bai</note> seven-character quatrains. Once you have these three men as your foundation, you can then look at the works of Tao Yuanming, Ying Yang, Liu Zhen, Xie Lingyun, Ruan Ji, Yu Xin, Bao Zhao, and others. Since you are such a clever and bright person, in less than a year’s work, you need not worry about not becoming a venerable poet!" Hearing this, Xiangling smiled and said, "If that is the case, good Miss, please bring that book out for me. I will take it back and read a few poems at night." Upon hearing this, Daiyu ordered Zijuan to bring the five-character regulated poems of Wang the Right Vice-President <note>Wang Wei</note> and handed them to Xiangling, saying, "Only look at those with red circles; those are the ones I have selected. Read them one by one. If there is something you do not understand, ask your mistress; or if you run into me, I will explain it to you."

Xiangling took the poems and returned to the Garden of All-Pervading Fragrance <note>the residence of Xue Baochai</note>. Ignoring all other matters, she simply sat under the lamp and began reading them poem by poem. Baochai urged her several times to go to sleep, but she would not. Seeing her such devotion, Baochai had no choice but to let her be.

One day, just as Daiyu had finished washing and grooming herself, she saw Xiangling approaching with a smile to return the book and ask for the poems of Du Fu. Daiyu smiled and asked, "How many poems do you remember?" Xiangling laughed, "I have read all of those marked with red circles." Daiyu asked, "Have you gained any insights?" Xiangling smiled and said, "I have indeed gained some, but I do not know if they are correct. Let me tell them to you."

<summary>Xiangling asks Lin Daiyu to teach her the art of poetry, and Daiyu provides a curriculum focusing on Tang masters Wang Wei, Du Fu, and Li Bai. Xiangling begins her studies with great devotion, staying up late to read and returning to discuss her initial insights.</summary>
<keywords>Xiangling, Lin Daiyu, poetry education, Wang Wei, Du Fu, Li Bai, poetic theory, Dream of the Red Chamber</keywords>
